Geometric entanglement entropy is treated as a thermodynamic potential, and horizons as finite-capacity information systems. When this capacity is saturated, local semiclassical descriptions break down without affecting underlying unitary dynamics. This defines a representational, not dynamical, transition, where configurations persist but cannot be locally encoded.
